issue.description:
CommandRegex, both front-ends, deny-only for v1 (Tier 1 -- stateless, decidable from a single invocation: the command text alone shows whether -a/--all is present, or whether trailing pathspec arguments exist after -m/--message). Denies git commit calls that would commit the entire staged index rather than an explicit path set: git commit -a/--all, and bare git commit -m "..." (or --message) with no trailing pathspec arguments.

This is a distinct gap from CLAUDE.md's existing git-staging rule. That rule already bans git add -A/git add ./git commit -a -- but an agent following it precisely (staging only explicit paths via git add <paths>) can still sweep unrelated pre-staged content into its commit if it then runs a bare git commit -m with no pathspec of its own, since git commit with no path arguments commits the full current index, not just what was just added.

Root incident (2026-08-14, commitgraph, worker claude-code-glm-5-adr018, bead cg-194i4a): git add containers/migration-worker/migrator.py containers/migration-worker/test_migrator.py (correct, precise staging) followed by bare git commit -m "..." produced commit 2bcbfe2, which also included ~430 unrelated lines from containers/queue-api/internal/{server,storage}/blocklist*.go -- pre-staged by a different concurrent NEEDLE worker in the same shared checkout. The worker self-corrected (git reset --soft HEAD~1 plus a clean re-commit passing the same two paths to git commit itself, landing as 1543ae2, verified never pushed to origin) before this rule existed to catch it mechanically -- this bead exists so the correction doesn't have to depend on a worker noticing on its own next time.

Distinct failure mode from Stale-HEAD push guard (irrevers-8cff8cf4): that catches pushing on top of remote state that's since moved. This catches unrelated staged content riding into a commit within the same shared tree, before any push ever happens -- the exact incident class that guard's own description already flags as outside its scope.

Redirect: deny + actionable reason ("pass the same file paths to git commit that you passed to git add -- git commit <paths> -m \"...\""). Not updatedInput: Tier 1 has no memory of what a prior git add in the same session actually staged (that is Tier 2 territory, per Architecture), so the correct pathspec to substitute is not derivable from the git commit call's own text -- per docs/notes/redirect-not-just-block.md, updatedInput is reserved for transformations that preserve intent through a derivable safer mechanism, which this is not. Stays deny with an actionable message, same tier/channel as its git-pack siblings (force-push detection, Stale-HEAD push guard).

Applies to all repos, not just known-shared-checkout ones (user direction 2026-08-14) -- explicit pathspecs on git commit have no real downside in an uncontended repo, so this is not scoped narrowly the way the beads-conjunction check is.

Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1 git pack -- also needs Architecture's pack list and Phase 1's rule-set prose updated to name this rule (not yet done as of this bead's creation).
issue.title: git pack: commit-without-pathspec guard

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md (562 lines, 5 gap-review rounds complete as of 2026-08-13)

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks/redirects irreversible operations, extending org-rule-guard.py's coverage. Full decomposition: 44 beads total (28 created directly from Phase 0-3's plan content, plus 16 pre-existing beads from two /plan-idea-gen ideation runs, retroactively wired with blocker edges to the infrastructure they actually depend on).

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path (icg-ci pipeline, release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, self-updater, release-cutting runbook): 6 beads (icg-4me, icg-52j, icg-1dk, icg-4nu, icg-2nw, icg-24g)
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, both front-ends where applicable: 8 infrastructure beads (icg-4vq, icg-2jd, icg-1k0, icg-3my, icg-3q6, icg-6bg, icg-rik, icg-51o) + 8 new content-pack beads (icg-6tj, icg-1bav, icg-4bra, icg-25sg, icg-4nt2, icg-14ff, icg-u34c, icg-shs8) + 2 pre-existing content beads (icg-2m8 git stale-HEAD, icg-1vj misc deprecated-bead-CLI)
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state: 3 beads (icg-1seg state-store, icg-2eu0 flush-before-pull, icg-20ja flush-before-repair)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness: 3 beads (icg-25u2 updatedInput force-push, icg-50ya additionalContext+Codex-fallback, icg-4338 value-derivation helpers)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists: 9 pre-existing beads (icg-rri, icg-ncf, icg-2ck, icg-l75, icg-1tj, icg-z5n, icg-2i8, icg-59u, icg-d3i)
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists: 6 pre-existing beads (icg-4p8, icg-2m8 [counted in Phase 1], icg-4bu, icg-3xz, icg-4mu, icg-53q) + 1 done directly (README non-goals section, no bead)

## Flagged gap from decomposition review (fallback role, per user direction)
One real gap found reviewing plan.md against the 44-bead decomposition: icg-4bu's fail-closed transition has an explicit open implementation question in Architecture (docs/plan/plan.md lines ~73-87) -- whether Claude Code's/Codex's own hook-timeout/hook-error config can substitute for a dedicated watchdog process, avoiding the 'standing daemon' architecture ideation explicitly killed elsewhere (Lens-1 idea #69). This verification step (checking both harnesses' actual hook specs) isn't its own trackable bead anywhere -- it's prose inside icg-4bu's blocking Architecture discussion. Whoever picks up icg-4bu should do this verification FIRST, before assuming a watchdog is needed; if neither harness supports it, icg-4bu needs to either accept the standing-daemon cost or get re-scoped. Not spinning up a separate bead for this since it's a research step gating one specific bead's approach, not independent work -- flagged here instead per genesis-bead-as-fallback role.

Everything else reviewed against plan.md's Architecture/Components/Data Models/Phases sections maps cleanly onto an existing bead -- no other coverage gaps found.

issue.description: In the beginning, the guard dying (e.g. OOM-killed mid-check) does NOT halt the fleet -- fails open, matching org-rule-guard.py's existing philosophy. As the guard's reliability is validated over time, shift to a fail-closed posture where the fleet can't run without the guard being healthy. Graduation signal ties to the poison-pill auto-rollback mechanism (icg-2ck) already tracking per-release deny-rate health -- e.g. N consecutive releases with zero poison-pill triggers -- rather than inventing a new maturity signal from scratch; exact threshold TBD at implementation time. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #6 (policy per user direction 2026-08-13).
issue.title: Graduated fail-open to fail-closed policy for guard crashes

issue.description: Every deny verdict automatically appends its command as a new regression-suite case (hook a --record-as-test path into the deny-dispatch code, writing to tests/regression/<pack-id>.cases). From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #1.
